t.7.24.1: Returning homeward, the evil-souled Rāvaṇa, filled with delight, carried off along the way maidens of kings, of ṛṣis, of gods and of Gandharvas.
t.7.24.2: Whatever beautiful maiden or woman the Rākṣasa saw, he killed her kinsfolk and placed her in his aerial chariot.
t.7.24.3: There Rāvaṇa seized the maidens of the Pannagas and Yakṣas, of men and Rākṣasas, and of the Daityas and Dānavas.
t.7.24.4: Long-haired and with exceedingly lovely limbs, their faces like the full moon, all those young women were overcome by grief and bowed down by the weight of their breasts.
t.7.24.5: There, trembling and stricken with grief, they shed tear-born water, like flames of fire, sprung from the fire of sorrow and from fear.
t.7.24.7: One woman, sorely stricken with grief, thought, "He may even kill me." Remembering their mothers, fathers, brothers, sons and fathers-in-law too, the women, overwhelmed by sorrow and grief, lamented together.
t.7.24.6: Set ablaze by the sighs of those sighing women, the Puṣpaka, with fire pent up within it, shone like the sacred agnihotra fire.
t.7.24.8: How indeed will my son manage without me? How will my mother, how will my brother fare, sunk in an ocean of grief?
t.7.24.9: Alas, what shall I do without my husband, who is my god? O Death, be gracious, I beg you: lead me to the abode of Yama.
t.7.24.10: What evil deed, I wonder, did I commit long ago in another body, that I have now been violated by him and have fallen into an ocean of grief?
t.7.24.11: Indeed, I see no end now to my own sorrow here. Alas, shame on the world of men! Truly, there is nothing more base than this.
t.7.24.12: Since my weak kinsmen have been destroyed by the mighty Rāvaṇa, just as the stars are blotted out by the rising sun.
t.7.24.13: Alas, this exceedingly mighty Rākṣasa delights in the means of slaying! Alas, he himself does not recognize his own wicked self.
t.7.24.14: The valour of this wicked-souled one is in every way fitting indeed; but this deed, the violation of others' wives, is unbefitting.
t.7.24.15: Since this evil-minded one delights in the wives of others, Rāvaṇa shall therefore meet his death on account of a woman.
t.7.24.16: Then, cursed by those women, virtuous and devoted to their husbands, who stood firm on the path of righteousness, he was robbed of his splendour and became utterly lustreless.
t.7.24.17: While the women were lamenting thus, Rāvaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas, entered the city of Laṅkā, honored by the night-wanderers.
t.7.24.18: Then the sister of the king of the Rākṣasas, deeply distressed, fell at his feet and began to speak.
t.7.24.19: Then Rāvaṇa, raising his sister up and consoling her, said: "What is this, good lady? You should tell me quickly."
t.7.24.20: That rākṣasī, her eyes choked with tears, spoke these words: "I am struck down, O king! By you, mighty one, I have been made a widow."
t.7.24.21: O king, these Daityas known as the Kālakeyas, of great strength and valour, were slain by you in battle through your prowess.
t.7.24.22: There my husband, dearer to me even than life, was slain; that beloved one was slain there by you, my own brother, who behaved like an enemy.
t.7.24.24: Surely a son-in-law ought to be protected by you, even in battles; yet having slain him in combat with your own hand, O king, are you not ashamed?
t.7.24.23: O king, I have been struck down here by you yourself, my own kinsman; I shall now endure the sorrow and the very name of widowhood that you have given me.
t.7.24.25: Thus addressed by his sister, who was crying out in distress, the Rākṣasa comforted her and spoke these words, beginning with conciliation.
t.7.24.26: Enough of despair, dear child; you need have no fear at all. I shall always gratify you with special marks of honour and with gifts.
t.7.24.27: In battle, frenzied and distracted, eager for victory and loosing my arrows, I cannot tell my own people from the enemy in the fighting, O fair one. That is why your husband was slain by me in the fray, O sister.
t.7.24.28: Whatever is fitting at this time, that I shall do for your good: stay by the side of your brother Khara, who is established in sovereign power.
t.7.24.29: Your brother will be lord of fourteen thousand rākṣasas of great might, commanding them on the march and in the bestowing of gifts.
t.7.24.31: Let this hero go swiftly to protect the Daṇḍakas; the mighty Dūṣaṇa shall be the commander of his forces.
t.7.24.30: There your brother Khara, the mighty son of your mother's sister, will always carry out whatever word you yourself speak.
t.7.24.33: Having spoken thus, Daśagrīva assigned to him an army: fourteen thousand Rākṣasas able to take any form at will.
t.7.24.32: For that forest region was cursed long ago by the angry Uśanas; it will become a dwelling place of the Rākṣasas, there is no doubt.
t.7.24.34: Surrounded by all those Rākṣasas of terrifying appearance, Khara, fearing nothing from any quarter, swiftly set out for the Daṇḍakas.
t.7.24.35: There he ruled over a kingdom from which every thorn had been struck away, and Śūrpaṇakhā, well pleased, dwelt in the Daṇḍaka forest.
